subject: On‑prem VPC deploy: annotated runbook & operator walkthrough
messages:
From: Paul Jensen <pjensen@oncecloud.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, infra-team@oncecloud.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On‑prem VPC deploy — initial ask for operator runbook and demarc sample

Laura / Redwood team —

Thanks for the meeting earlier. OnceCloud is lining up the on‑prem racks for our pilot and we need one combined deliverable from Redwood: an operator‑facing runbook that shows the control‑plane / data‑plane demarc, expected BGP sessions, NAT/egress options, and a flattened diagram we can hand to the colo operator.

Key asks:
- A single‑page diagram that shows where Redwood's control plane sits (public vs customer‑managed), which IPs we need to source, and relevant firewall rules.
- A short checklist for cutover: L2 handoff, BGP keepalives, MTU recommendations, and a fallback path.
- One example packet flow for inference requests (client -> ingress -> runtime node -> egress telemetry) for our networking team to test.

Can you produce something by May 29 so we can book the colo change window on June 2? Attachments welcome (PDF/PNG).

Paul
Paul Jensen
Network Ops Lead, OnceCloud
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Jensen <pjensen@oncecloud.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, infra-team@oncecloud.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem VPC deploy — initial ask for operator runbook and demarc sample

Paul —

We can do that. I’ll take point on the deliverable and loop in Neha for the low‑level control/data separation details and Marcus for the deployment checklist. Plan: deliver an "annotated runbook" PDF + one flattened diagram + an operator checklist spreadsheet by end of day May 29.

A couple quick clarifications so we scope correctly:
- Do you want the control plane to be reachable from OnceCloud management LAN (private peering) or over a public endpoint? That changes the recommended firewall/ACL guidance.
- Any hard MTU constraints in the colo? 1500 is fine for our test but if jumbo frames are used we’ll note it.

If you confirm the control plane reachability I’ll lock the runbook to that option and mark the alternative as an appendix.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Deployments, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, pjensen@oncecloud.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, infra-team@oncecloud.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem VPC deploy — initial ask for operator runbook and demarc sample

Paul / Laura —

Quick technical notes for the runbook (will be reflected in the annotated PDF):
- Control plane: we recommend a customer‑facing TLS endpoint hosted in the VPC (HTTPS with client cert optional) + a lightweight management tunnel (mutual TLS) for health checks. For OnceCloud pilot, public endpoint with ACLs to OnceCloud management CIDRs is okay; private peering is preferred for long term.
- BGP: we expect a single eBGP session from the customer edge to the inference edge. Localpref and advertisement scope will be documented; keep community tagging simple (no custom AS prepends required).
- Egress: default NAT at the edge cluster egress node unless you opt into a routed public IP pool — we’ll call out both options and show packet flows for each.
- KV cache: control plane never touches KV cache; we include diagram showing KV cache stays within runtime nodes (data plane).

I’ll add an example tcpdump snippet and a simple sequence diagram for the request path (client -> LB -> runtime -> telemetry sink).

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Paul Jensen <pjensen@oncecloud.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, infra-team@oncecloud.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem VPC deploy — initial ask for operator runbook and demarc sample

Thanks — two follow ups from the colo side:
1) Our colo will not allow inbound management over the public internet for that rack. We can provision a private L3 peer if Redwood supports it. That means private peering preferred.
2) For BGP we need expected community tags so our route filters can accept only the prefixes you will originate (safety). Can you include a sample BGP export table and the exact prefixes Redwood will advertise?

We’ll plan the June 2 window once we have the private peering instructions + diagram.

Paul
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Jensen <pjensen@oncecloud.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, infra-team@oncecloud.com, contracts@oncecloud.com
Date: Thu, 29 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Deliverable: annotated runbook + flat diagrams for OnceCloud pilot (attached)

Paul —

Attached: annotated-runbook-v2.pdf, vpc-control-dataflow-flatmap.png, operator-checklist.xlsx. High level summary of what we delivered:
- Control plane model: private L3 peering (customer‑managed) documented in section 3 with peering parameters and ACL examples. Appendix A contains the public endpoint fallback.
- BGP: we will originate the following prefixes for the pilot: 198.51.100.0/26 (ingress LB), 198.51.100.64/27 (egress NAT pool). Community tag: RW-INF:1001 for pilot prefixes. Sample export table and route map included in section 4.
- Packet flow: two examples included (NAT path and routed public IP path) with tcpdump keys you can run at the colo to validate flows.
- Operational checklist: L2 handoff verification, BFD keepalive sanity checks, MTU confirmation step, rollback path to upstream NAT if new routes fail.

Links: full folder with raw diagrams and a one‑page cutout for the colo operator is at https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_runbook_OnceCloud. I also opened OPS-4921 for the cutover runbook acceptance test.

Next steps we propose:
- OnceCloud to confirm private peering details (ASN, peer IPs, VLAN) and we’ll produce the final peering config snippets.
- On acceptance we’ll shift the operator checklist to your change window template and join the pre‑cutover call.

If you want a short walkthrough (15m) for your colo operators I can run it tomorrow morning.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Deployments, Redwood Inference

Attachments: annotated-runbook-v2.pdf (34 pages, PDF), vpc-control-dataflow-flatmap.png (PNG), operator-checklist.xlsx (Excel)
